reference.source: Sherlock's Diseases of the Liver and Biliary System / EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines
clinicalPearls: Characterised by multiple bile-duct-derived cysts scattered through the liver parenchyma, often numbering in the dozens or hundreds
Isolated autosomal dominant PLD is linked to mutations in genes such as PRKCSH and SEC63, and cysts also occur as part of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)
Most patients are asymptomatic, but massive hepatomegaly can cause abdominal distension, early satiety, breathlessness, and pain
Liver synthetic function is usually preserved even with extensive cystic replacement
Complications include cyst haemorrhage, infection, rupture, and compression of adjacent structures such as the bile ducts, portal vein, or inferior vena cava
It is more prevalent and cysts are larger in women, with growth influenced by oestrogen exposure
Management ranges from observation to cyst aspiration/sclerotherapy, fenestration, hepatic resection, or transplantation for severe symptomatic disease; somatostatin analogues can reduce liver volume
reference.pathophysiology: Polycystic liver disease arises from abnormal proliferation of the biliary epithelium and defective ductal plate remodelling, producing fluid-filled cysts derived from biliary microhamartomas that lose continuity with the biliary tree. In isolated autosomal dominant disease, mutations in genes including PRKCSH (encoding hepatocystin) and SEC63 disrupt glycoprotein processing and protein translocation in cholangiocytes, promoting cyst formation. Cysts also accompany ADPKD (PKD1/PKD2). Progressive cyst growth, modulated by oestrogen and cyclic AMP-driven fluid secretion, leads to hepatomegaly and mass-effect complications while sparing hepatocellular function.
additionalDifferentials: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease with hepatic cysts
Caroli disease and congenital hepatic fibrosis
Autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease with hepatic involvement
additionalInvestigations: Abdominal ultrasound as first-line imaging for cyst number and size
CT or MRI to characterise cyst burden, complications, and vascular/biliary compression
Renal imaging to assess for coexisting ADPKD
Serum tumour markers and cyst fluid analysis if a cystic neoplasm is suspected
Genetic testing (PRKCSH, SEC63, PKD1/PKD2) in familial or syndromic cases
redFlags: Fever and localised pain suggesting cyst infection
Sudden severe pain from cyst haemorrhage or rupture
Jaundice or portal hypertension from biliary or vascular compression
Lower-limb oedema or Budd-Chiari-like features from inferior vena cava/hepatic vein compression
reference.prognosis: Overall prognosis is good because hepatocellular function is generally preserved; symptoms relate to liver volume and complications, and even severely affected patients can be managed with volume-reducing procedures or, rarely, transplantation.
pitfalls: Failing to look for coexisting renal cysts and distinguish ADPKD from isolated PLD
Mistaking a cystic neoplasm or hydatid cyst for a simple polycystic cyst
Aspirating a cyst without sclerotherapy, leading to rapid recurrence
Attributing abnormal liver tests to the cysts rather than seeking another cause
references: Sherlock's Diseases of the Liver and Biliary System
EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines on the management of cystic liver disease
management: Most patients need no intervention; treat only symptomatic mass-effect disease, with reassurance given preserved hepatocellular function
Volume-reducing procedures for symptomatic hepatomegaly, including cyst aspiration with sclerotherapy for a dominant cyst, laparoscopic fenestration, or hepatic resection
Somatostatin analogues to reduce cyst volume and symptoms in selected patients
Advise avoidance or minimisation of oestrogen-containing therapies, which promote cyst growth in women
Manage complications with antibiotics for cyst infection and treatment of cyst haemorrhage, rupture, or compression of the bile ducts, portal vein or inferior vena cava
Liver transplantation for massive, refractory disease with intractable symptoms
Assess for coexisting autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease and provide genetic counselling in familial cases
